audit_scope.description: Ethereum consensus and execution layer components covering beacon chain operations (EIP-4736 BLSToExecutionChange), EVM execution (EIP-7516 BLOBBASEFEE opcode, Cancun stack operations), and smart contract deployment (EIP-170 size limits, EIP-1716 hardfork)

components.name: Beacon Node
components.description: Consensus layer node handling BLSToExecutionChange messages and P2P broadcast

components.name: EVM
components.description: Ethereum Virtual Machine executing smart contract bytecode and opcodes

components.name: State Trie
components.description: Ethereum state storage for contracts and account data

components.name: P2P Network Layer
components.description: Peer-to-peer networking for block and message propagation

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via BLS Withdrawal Change Submission
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange message submission to community repository and P2P broadcast
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators are authenticated through BLS signature verification over withdrawal credential changes. While they must prove ownership of BLS keys, they could potentially submit malicious or conflicting withdrawal changes. The trust model relies on cryptographic verification and community-validated broadcast files to prevent conflicts.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator loading broadcast files
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Broadcast file configuration and loading into beacon node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators voluntarily load broadcast files to filter BLSToExecutionChange messages. They are semi-trusted because they control node configuration and could choose not to participate in filtering, but they cannot inject invalid data as all messages must pass signature verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Claim Submitter to community repository
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange claim submission to community repository
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Claim submitters are untrusted external actors who may submit arbitrary claims. All claims must pass cryptographic validation (BLS signature verification, validator index checks) and community verification before acceptance into broadcast files.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange message propagation via beacon chain P2P network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are untrusted and may send malicious or conflicting BLSToExecutionChange messages. The beacon node applies filtering based on locally loaded broadcast files and cryptographic validation to reject conflicting messages and prevent attacker message propagation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via transaction submission
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract creation transaction submission with initialization bytecode
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Contract deployers are untrusted external users or contracts submitting contract creation transactions. They can submit arbitrary initialization code, which is executed in the EVM sandbox. EIP-170 enforces MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes) to prevent DoS attacks via oversized contracts. Failed deployments consume gas but cannot corrupt state.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network propagating blocks
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block propagation via Ethereum P2P network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The P2P network propagates blocks containing transactions and contract creations. Network peers are untrusted and may propagate invalid blocks. All blocks undergo full validation including contract size limit checks (EIP-170) to ensure consensus rules are followed. Invalid blocks are rejected without state changes.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: BLSToExecutionChange message submission and P2P broadcast interface
boundary_edges.security_assumption: BLS signature verification ensures only the holder of the validator's BLS key can authorize withdrawal credential changes. The system assumes BLS keys are not compromised. Community-validated broadcast files provide additional protection against conflicting messages by enabling nodes to filter based on pre-submitted claims.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon node configuration interface for broadcast file loading
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The security model assumes voluntary participation by node operators in loading and honoring broadcast file filtering. Without widespread participation, the protection mechanism has limited effectiveness. Node operators are trusted to load correctly verified broadcast files, but cannot bypass signature validation for incoming messages.

All submitted claims undergo cryptographic validation including filename format checks, validator index verification against consensus layer state, BLS signature verification, and single-operation-per-validator constraints. The community repository verification process is assumed to be performed correctly and honestly to prevent invalid claims from entering broadcast files.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon chain P2P network message propagation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The beacon node applies defense-in-depth: (1) cryptographic validation of all BLSToExecutionChange signatures, (2) optional filtering based on broadcast files to reject messages conflicting with pre-submitted claims, (3) single-operation-per-validator enforcement at protocol level. Messages from untrusted peers cannot bypass these validations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction submission and contract creation interface
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The EVM sandbox enforces strict contract size limits (MAX_CODE_SIZE = 24576 bytes per EIP-170) to prevent DoS attacks on light clients. Size limit violations trigger out-of-gas exceptions consuming all remaining gas, preventing state changes. The limit applies to returned deployment bytecode, not initialization code. All gas costs are prepaid, ensuring failed deployments cannot exhaust node resources without payment.

All blocks received from the network undergo full validation including verification that all contract creations satisfy the MAX_CODE_SIZE limit (EIP-170). Invalid blocks are rejected without state changes. The bounded verification time enabled by size limits prevents DoS attacks via blocks containing oversized contracts. Consensus rules are uniformly enforced across all client implementations.

coverage_analysis.notes: All external entities have corresponding boundary edges with explicit security assumptions. Three files (EIP-7516 BLOBBASEFEE opcode, Cancun stack operations, EIP-1716 hardfork) contained no external entities as they model internal EVM execution and consensus rule changes without external interaction points.
